quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Technical writers write technical materials such as equipment manuals, appendices, or operating and maintenance instructions, and may help with layout.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Technical Writers) include Engineering Writer, Global Technical Writer, Principal Technical Writer and Technical Report Writer.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a technical writer does
paragraphs: Technical writers write technical materials such as equipment manuals, appendices, or operating and maintenance instructions, and may help with layout.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Technical Writers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Organise material and write to set standards of order and clarity.
Edit, standardise or revise material prepared by other writers or staff.
Follow developments in a field to see when published material needs revising.
Choose the photographs, drawings, diagrams and charts that illustrate the material.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: BA (Bachelor of Arts); Content Writer.
Less common routes on the map: B.Sc (Bachelor of Science); B.Tech (Bachelor of Technology).
